Only name/dirs/files with name/path/size survive; producer extras (relith-rez offset/time/type) are dropped so the native client and agents see one shape. Depth 64 and 200,000 nodes bound recursion and memory below the 4 MiB stdout default; a malformed node fails the whole preview rather than showing a partial tree.

Ported from `orchestrator/server/formats.mjs` with F156 (spec 129); the JavaScript this describes is gone. The record it is judged against is `orchestrator/tests/preview-corpus.json`, where 'a tree preview whose node is the wrong shape' is the malformed-node case.

anchor.snippet: pub fn read_bytes(root_id: &str, root_path: &str, data: &Value) -> Result<Value, Fail> {

entries.note:
Open first, then fstat the handle, then confine a fresh resolution of the same relative path and require the same dev/inode as the opened handle; a swap between resolution and open is reported as a 409 rather than served. Node has no frealpath, so inode identity is the strongest confinement of what was actually opened.

Ported from `orchestrator/server/formats.mjs` with F156 (spec 129). The FIRST port dropped this: it resolved the name, stat'd the name and opened the name, which confines what the name pointed at rather than what was read. No corpus case could have caught it — the rule is about a race, and a record of answers has no case for one; this entry is what caught it, while the JavaScript still existed to compare against. Rust has no frealpath either, so the shape is the same: open, `File::metadata` (fstat on the handle), re-resolve, compare. `same_file` is dev+ino on unix and size+mtime elsewhere, because an open handle's identity is not stable API on Windows — a weaker check there, stated rather than hidden. The predicate is unit-tested; the race is not stageable.
